subject: Life Skills
title: Source Checking 101
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Source Checking 101.

hook.text: A Stanford study found that 82% of students couldn't tell a real news site from a fake one.

buildup.text: Anyone can publish online. A professional-looking website costs less than a meal to create.

discovery.text: Check who wrote it, when it was published, and whether other reputable outlets confirm the claim.

twist.text: Even credible sources make mistakes. Cross-referencing three independent sources multiplies reliability.

climax.text: Use the SIFT method: Stop, Investigate the source, Find better coverage, Trace the original claim.

punchline.text: Don't trust the article. Trust the evidence.

quiz.question: What does the SIFT method help you do?
